figures.title: Gallbladder: CHST4 immunohistochemistry
figures.caption: Gallbladder tissue stained for carbohydrate sulfotransferase 4 (CHST4). Brown: CHST4 protein. Blue: cell nuclei (hematoxylin counterstain).
figures.alt: Microscope image of gallbladder tissue with CHST4 protein stained brown and cell nuclei stained blue.
figures.credit: Image from the Human Protein Atlas 25.1 (proteinatlas.org): Gallbladder: CHST4 immunohistochemistry, https://images.proteinatlas.org/21955/148702_A_5_4.jpg. CC BY 4.0.

figures.title: Gallbladder
figures.caption: The gallbladder stores and concentrates bile, and releases it into the two-way cystic duct when it is needed by the small intestine.
figures.alt: This figure shows the gallbladder and its major parts are labeled.
figures.credit: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax. Figure “Gallbladder”, section 23.6 Accessory Organs in Digestion: The Liver, Pancreas, and Gallbladder. CC BY 4.0. Access for free at https://openstax.org/books/anatomy-and-physiology-2e/pages/1-introduction
